newsitem.title: new zealand: CRICKET-NZ'S HARRIS HITS OUT VS SRI LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ'S HARRIS HITS OUT VS SRI LANKA.

text.p: Chris Harris saved New Zealand's blushes during their one-day cricket international against Sri Lanka on Tuesday.

The allrounder took 18 runs off the final five deliveries from left arm seamer Chaminda Vaas to push his side over the 200-run threshold after they were invited to bat by Sri Lankan captain Arjuna Ranatunga.
New Zealand finished on 201 for nine from their allotted 50 overs, thanks to Harris, who smacked an unbeaten 38 from just 37 deliveries.
Harris and tailender Heath Davis put on 31 for the last wicket in just 17 minutes after New Zealand looked unlikely to even challenge the double century mark.
Harris finished the innings in style with a six over wide long on to take full advantage of Ranatunga's surprising decision to employ Vaas for the last over.
Until that point the tourists had held the upperhand after their slow bowlers appreciated a pitch providing low, slow bounce.
The Kiwis were slow until Harris' late heroics as he went on to topscore in an otherwise disappointing batting performance.

All of New Zealand's specialist batsmen made starts but none achieved much more, and Sri Lanka kept a tight rein on the run rateafter Kiwi openers Nathan Astle and Bryan Young started soundly enough at four runs an over.

But tall left arm seamer Nuwan Zoysa celebrated his first international one-day appearance to remove the two openers, Astle going first for 23 when Roshan Mahanama pulled off an excellent diving catch in the covers, and Young following 10 runs later for 21 when Zoysa pegged back his leg stump.

Matt Horne played all over a fullish delivery from offspinner Muttiah Muralitharan to be bowled after making 13 and captain Stephen Fleming's run out for 31 reduced New Zealand to 104 for four in the 27th over.

Left arm spinner Sanath Jayasuriya helped tighten the screws further by having dangerman Chris Cairns caught at backward square leg by Kumar Dharmasena and then accepting a gift return catch from Adam Parore to see the Kiwis struggling at 142 for six in the 37th over.
The Sri Lankans had been most successful in restraining the normally freescoring Cairns, his contribution of 27 coming off 63 deliveries, none of which he managed to guide to the boundary.
Jayasuriya, whose darting deliveries proved difficult to score off, picked up his third wicket when snapping up a low return catch from Simon Doull.
He finished with the excellent figures of three for 26 from 10 overs. Offspinner Muralitharan had two for 42 and Dharmasena gave up just 32 runs from his 10.
